goals.outcome: Verify changes to fixed-width interface and expiry calculations with less complete engineering effort.
goals.binding_constraint: Proof updates, byte-order ambiguities and negative-case review can dominate maintenance even when exact semantics are simple.
goals.missing_move_question: Can a new proof tactic remove repetitive congruence work without weakening the independent JavaScript and bit-vector references?
goals.beneficiary: MONTREAL.AI maintainers of the registered FRONTIER expiry decoder
goals.strong_alternative: Lean explicit congruence plus current JavaScript regression and independent finite reference
goals.experiment: Freeze one fresh real protocol change; give the same diff and tests to the old explicit-proof route and new +uf route; independently score blinded byte-order and overflow mutations and total review effort.
goals.falsifier: No correctness or review-cost improvement over the ordinary explicit-proof route on the same accepted change.

goals.outcome: Make recurring bounded agent decisions cheaper and portable without losing accepted outcomes.
goals.binding_constraint: Repeated broad-model inference may dominate costs, but deterministic routing and compiled all-System-2 workflows can already be competitive.
goals.missing_move_question: Can a reusable decision-point compiler preserve quality across distinct workflows where competent deterministic routing fails?
goals.beneficiary: MONTREAL.AI's authorized research-triage and engineering-review operators
goals.strong_alternative: Existing typed deterministic router, competent compiled workflow and strong direct model under identical permissions
goals.experiment: Freeze fresh held-out routing cases in two independently reviewed workflows; test direct, conventional compiled and candidate System-1 routes with full fallback and maintenance costs.
goals.falsifier: Material acceptance regression or no complete-cost improvement against the strongest compiled or deterministic route.
goals.rights: Only authorized public or redacted workflow records; no automatic customer action, paid model inference or new deployment.
goals.future_trigger: A verified release or separately reviewed research record supplies an accessible decision-specialist capability.

goals.outcome: Increase the throughput of an existing accepted inference workload without violating its latency and quality constraints.
goals.binding_constraint: High aggregate throughput may fail per-user latency, quality, reliability or cost limits at realistic concurrency.
goals.missing_move_question: Can revised scheduler and cache behavior eliminate a bottleneck without new hardware or a degraded acceptance contract?
goals.beneficiary: MONTREAL.AI Endpoint Lab and HARNESS operators
goals.strong_alternative: Current measured serving stack, tuned configuration and tested direct execution under identical traffic

goals.falsifier: No higher accepted workload throughput after complete operational costs or a violation of p90 latency or quality.
goals.rights: Authorized traffic and local instrumentation only; no external API spend without approval.
goals.future_trigger: A published scheduler/runtime release materially alters reproducible serving behavior.

goals.outcome: Deploy a verified scientific/agent capability on previously unsupported or impractically costly hardware.
goals.binding_constraint: Device support, kernels and memory footprint constrain portable local execution.

goals.outcome: Make one bounded scientific decision process repeatable using a verified, portable instrument.
goals.binding_constraint: Specialized scientific data and validation requirements may make general agent execution excessive and error-prone.

goals.falsifier: The direct specialist ties or exceeds the new instrument on accepted outcomes with lower complete effort.
goals.rights: Public reusable datasets or independently authorized scientific records only.
